represents: Google Cloud IAM and identity-federation administration across an organisation's projects: Terraform (a service account impersonated through GitHub Workload Identity Federation) granting NAMED groups and service accounts scoped roles on projects, buckets, Cloud Run, Secret Manager and Pub/Sub; GKE Workload Identity bindings (serviceAccount:<project>.svc.id.goog[ns/ksa]); SA-to-SA token-creator grants; Workload Identity pools and providers for GitHub, GitLab and AWS that all carry attribute conditions (create begin/end entries, mapping-only and tightening updates); one repository's attribute.repository principalSet bound to its deploy SA; a workforce pool with OIDC and SAML providers that carry conditions, plus the corporate Microsoft Entra ID provider (tenant-specific issuer) created without one; workforce groups bound to read-only org roles and the platform-admins group to GKE admin on the prod folder; key hygiene; ADMIN_READ refresh; and, rarely, the intentionally public marketing site on Cloud Run. Template weights deliberately over-sample the activity adjacent to the rules in adjacent_to (and their documented false-positive classes), so a rule's hits and rate_per_10k on this slice are corpus figures, not a production rate.
provenance: synthetic; shapes from the Cloud Audit Logs LogEntry / AuditLog reference (protoPayload.authenticationInfo incl. serviceAccountDelegationInfo, requestMetadata, authorizationInfo, serviceData.policyDelta.bindingDeltas, request/response, operation first/last), the IAM workload- and workforce-identity-federation docs (provider request fields, principal identifiers) and this repo's TRR9014 / TRR9018 / TRR9020 fixtures. Org id follows the repo fixtures; project ids / numbers are made up; principals are role handles at example.com; IdPs are idp.example.com / sso.example.org; addresses RFC 5737. The Entra ID workforce provider omits attributeCondition because the field is optional for workforce providers (gcloud 570 'iam workforce-pools providers create-oidc --help': --attribute-condition is an optional flag, 'If unspecified, all valid authentication credential will be accepted'), and Google requires a condition only where one issuer serves many tenants; a tenant-specific Entra issuer (login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0, the Azure slices' tenant) already limits the trust to the organisation. Request-body naming follows what each service actually logs: the legacy IAM admin service (CreateServiceAccount, CreateRole, keys) logs proto field names in snake_case with integer enums (account_id, service_account.display_name, role_id, included_permissions, stage: 2), while WorkforcePools.* and WorkloadIdentityPools.* log camelCase (workforcePoolId, workforcePoolProvider.attributeCondition, oidc.issuerUri, updateMask), as in the sanitized Cloud Audit Log captures in panther-analysis' GCP rule tests (gcp_service_account_or_keys_created, gcp_iam_custom_role_changes, gcp_workforce_pool_created_or_updated, gcp_workload_identity_pool_created_or_updated) and this repo's TRR9018 / TRR9020 fixtures. Org- and folder-level policies carry org / folder admin bindings, not a project's service agent.
